name: speed-quiet
title: Hooks and commands on a real archive
summary: How long an agent session waits for ctx. Hooks run on every session start, compaction and subagent start, so they are held to a 3-second limit and should take a small fraction of it.

metrics.label: Session start: rules and archive note
Before a search: the gate, session told
Before a command that is not a search: the gate
Read a turn with its neighbours

bar: every hook's slowest run under 1,000 ms
baseline: the 3-second limit Claude Code gives a hook, and the 1-second bar set here
meaning: Every hook takes 4 to 30 ms at the median and none came near the bar; the slowest single run was the compaction brief at 62 ms. The brief used to take 0.4 to 1.2 s on its first run: to find the last landing the person reported it read the text of every typed turn in the archive. It now finds the session's own documents first and reads only their turns. The gate adds about 5 ms to a search or shell command, most of which is the cost of starting a process. The two listing commands are typed by a person, not run by a hook, and are slower.
